prompt:
I need the front end for Shoalreach Campaign Keeper. A free, volunteer-maintained web tool that a community miniatures wargaming club uses to run its year-long narrative campaign across an invented archipelago, tracking who holds which region and where battles can happen next.

Who's using it: Tomasz Wierzbicki, 44, a school bus mechanic who volunteers as campaign organizer for the Harbor Street Wargames Club. The club meets Thursday nights in a church hall and has no budget beyond a $5 monthly member contribution. He knows the rules thoroughly but isn't technical; another member set the tool up for him.

What they're doing right now: It's Sunday evening after week 6 of 12. He has just entered the results of last Thursday's four battles, and two regions changed hands. Three players have since declared attacks for this week, and one of them, Dana's Saltborn raiders, claims to be striking the Gullrock lighthouse from a port that may no longer connect to it after the Vellmarsh fell. Before he sends the club its Thursday pairings, he has to work out which declared attacks are actually legal given adjacency, sea lanes and supply. He also has to settle which contested border should host the club's one large 3-table battle.

What's in the system at this point: An archipelago of 47 named regions across 6 islands, each with a terrain type (marsh, highland, reef, forest, port town) and a strategic value of 1 to 3. There are 14 sea lanes linking ports, two of them seasonal and closed until week 8. Nine players are split across 4 factions: Saltborn (3 players), Iron Covenant (2), Verdant Court (2) and the Drowned Kings (2). Each region records its current holder, the week it was taken, its garrison strength (0 to 5) and whether it is in supply. Battle history covers 23 battles so far, each with the week, the region, the players involved, the winner and margin of victory, and a short narrative note. The 3 pending attack declarations each name an origin region, a target, a declaring player and the time submitted. Faction totals stand at Saltborn 15 regions, Iron Covenant 12, Verdant Court 11, Drowned Kings 9.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
